requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The {impl} code covers each obligation, and tests cover the main cases and the `.md` edge case. One gap: no test marked for this requirement asserts the unchanged reference-badge links. **Implementation** - **Definition badge links and "See evidence"** (`replace_definitions`, src/lib.rs). For each `{req}` and `{example}` block it looks up the detail page with `plan.detail_path`. It renders the badge as `` and appends `

See evidence

` after the body. Both use `chapter_href`, and both are emitted only when a detail page exists, which is every definition. - **Detail page links back** (`render_detail_page`, src/index.rs). The header contains `[Requirements index](…)` only when an index path exists, and always contains `[View definition](…#habeas--)`. The anchor comes from `DefinitionKind::anchor`, which is the same id the badge carries. Index table rows link to the detail pages through `chapter_href` in `populate`. - **Reference badges** (`replace_inline_references`). They still link to the definition through `reference_badge` and `chapter_href`, with the same anchor. `reference_badge` itself is marked only with `requirements.references.book_badges`. I read that requirement's text, and it requires these badges to link to the definition, so it carries out the "continue to link" obligation. - **Names containing `.md`** (`chapter_href`). It rewrites `.md` to `%2Emd` in the whole generated href, path and anchor included. Every link above is built with it: badge, "See evidence", back-link, index row and reference badge. **Tests** - `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` (src/lib.rs) checks both a `req` and an `example` definition, plus the `rules.cli.mdbook` name. - It asserts the badge `id` and `href` and the "See evidence" paragraph, and that exactly 3 "See evidence" links appear. - It asserts the "View definition" back-link, including the `%2Emd` form. - It asserts that no "Requirements index" link appears when there is no index. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` (src/index.rs) covers the case where an index exists. It checks the badge href, the index row links, the "Requirements index" back-link followed by "View definition", and the definition anchor. - `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` (src/lib.rs) checks `chapter_href` directly in both directions, for the detail page and for the definition anchor. **Gap** - The reference-badge links are tested only by tests marked for `book_badges`, such as `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition`, not by tests marked for this requirement. I judged that acceptable because `book_badges` specifies that behavior.

text: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.

In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline or fenced, MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. A fenced reference MUST render its badge followed by its body as Markdown. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. Badges MAY be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a fenced reference's badge and body MAY be visually set apart from the surrounding text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge MAY show a help cursor to signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.
